predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the eastern arc of lowland Britain that the Chronica Gallica of 452 reports for 441 as handed over 'across a wide area' to the rule of the Saxons

successors.name: Kingdom of Mercia
successors.text: the East and West Midlands, Lincolnshire and parts of East Anglia: 104 of Mercia's 105 first-shape cells lie inside this state's corrected last shape (the 105th is Essex land)

successors.name: Kingdom of Wessex
successors.text: Hampshire, Surrey, Berkshire and Oxfordshire: the upper Thames and the south

successors.name: Kingdom of East Anglia
successors.text: Norfolk and Suffolk: Cliopatria's Kingdom of East Anglia row of 534 (52 cells, 12,391 km2) without the county of Essex, as the East Anglia dossier draws it; all of it lies inside this state's last…

successors.name: Kingdom of Deira
successors.text: the 5 cells of Cliopatria's Deira row of 534 that lie outside the Deira dossier's 555 shape (north Yorkshire, lat 53.8-54.6) and are still inside this state's last shape

ledger.x: 441: the Chronica Gallica of 452 records the British provinces passing to Saxon rule.

c. 450: Deira is established. Infobox 'Established: c. 450'; 'The kingdom, which was previously ruled by a British dynasty, was probably created in the third quarter of the fifth century when Anglian warriors invaded the Derwent Valley'; 'Archaeology suggests that the Anglian royal house was in place by the middle of…
480: Cliopatria widens the Anglo-Saxon shape by 144 cells, 89 of them once the Kent, Sussex and Deira land is left out; no page opened gives a date for it.
527: the East Saxons' kingdom is established.
533: the one Anglo-Saxon shape is replaced by named kingdoms.

wars.name: Hengist and Horsa's wars in Kent
wars.outcome: The Chronicle's Kentish campaign: 'in 455 Hengist and Horsa fought Vortigern at Ægelesthrep', where Horsa was killed; 'In 456 Hengest and Æsc battled the Britons at Crecganford'.

wars.name: Ælle's conquest of Sussex
wars.outcome: 'Ælle's battle with the British in 485 near the bank of Mercredesburne', then 'his siege of the Saxon Shore fort at Andredadsceaster' 'in 491 after which the inhabitants were massacred'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists in the period; every edge of the Saxon-held land is an approximation from settlement archaeology and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
